text: And I want to share with Mr Leong, when I say that the system has worked, actually the system has really worked.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I work very closely with the inmates and some of them are also under the CLTPA.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I could see that not only when they were detained but also the processes that they went through.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Some of them, their family members wrote to me, and I met the family members and I assured the family members that they would have the reviews done annually.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Some of them I met when they were released and the family members also shared with me, that some have transformed their lives.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: They shared that the whole process actually helped them.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: While no one likes our loved ones to be detained, nevertheless, Singapore's safety and security is of utmost importance.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Some of them even said that without this intervention, they would not be what they are today.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, as I shared earlier in my reply, it has worked well.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We would welcome any suggestions that you have given.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We will look at them, but I think what is key is that we want to look not only after Singaporeans.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We want to look after our country and we want to help those who are affected to get the right rehabilitation and reintegration journey.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We do not want to just change for something that is very theoretical.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: If we do not have something that has worked well, I think it is fine.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: But based on my ground experience, my engagement inside the prison, even outside when they are released, I feel it has worked well, Sir.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: I have two questions for the Minister of State.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Is it true that these detainees, especially for the first detention, they are only released three to four years after the first detention?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Whether this is true based on past practice?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Second question, if you look at the CLTPA, there are five big parts.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: One big chunk of Part 3 involves industrial actions by essential service workers.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: I just want to check in with the Minister of State whether MHA had reviewed this and see whether it is relevant in today's context, especially Part 1 of the Schedule.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: There will be opportunities for the Committees to assess these detainees based on the criminal activities in question, the detainees' antecedents, the detainees' conduct and response to the programmes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We not only look from the outward response.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We have a system where we really observe.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: For gang-related cases, some of the symptoms you cannot see physically, you need to sense, when you talk to them and when you see how they relate to the others, and you will have to monitor some of these things.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: These are things that we will continue to look at.

text: Are there any further clarifications for Minister of State Faishal?
